findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a render-settling strategy for the new `?expand=renderedFields` assertion (poll the rendered HTML until it reflects the pushed body, mirroring the harness's `_wait_until_*_reflects` discipline) so a not-yet-rendered read cannot flake as a fidelity regression.
evidence: The harness treats settling as mandatory: 'INDEX LAG. ... Every inbound cell therefore waits until a SEARCH REFLECTS THE NEW VALUE' (test_dc_mutations.py:23-29) and helpers `_wait_until_search_reflects`/`_wait_until_links_reflect`/`_wait_until_parent_map_reflects` (test_dc_mutations.py:78-159, 1514-1554)
Plan quote: 'asserts rendered HTML through ?expand=renderedFields ... so we verify what Jira actually interprets' — no wait/retry mentioned for the render read
ABSENCE: the plan gives no settling mechanism for the genuinely-new render read path it itself flags as 'a genuinely new fidelity check'
findings.finding: The plan's new `?expand=renderedFields` HTML assertion names no render-settling/retry strategy, unlike every existing read in this harness, which wraps Jira reads in a `_wait_until_*_reflects` poll because Jira reads (and its render pipeline) are eventually consistent.
findings.location: Approach (first bullet: 'asserts rendered HTML through ?expand=renderedFields') and Testing ('Live render fidelity')
scenarios: A description is pushed and a pass runs; the renderedFields HTML is read before Jira finishes (re)rendering the wiki body → the assertion sees stale/empty rendered markup and reports a false bridge defect (flaky red)
findings.suggested_fix: Add a bounded poll on the renderedFields HTML (analogous to `_wait_until_search_reflects`) that waits until the rendered markup contains the expected bold/heading/code-macro before asserting, with a timeout message that distinguishes render lag from an actual fidelity defect.

Endpoint granularity: a new endpoint (`expand=renderedFields`) on an already-used vendor (DC v2 REST) is a NEW integration whose response shape (renderedFields.description as an HTML string) and per-markup tag mapping are UNVERIFIED
Harness is linux/amd64-only (conftest _NOT_READY_MESSAGE; README arm64 note), so a wrong-shape HTML assertion is discoverable only in CI
findings.finding: The plan depends on a NEW external endpoint surface — reading rendered HTML from Jira DC 8.17.1 via `/rest/api/2/issue/{key}?expand=renderedFields` — that is asserted but never verified against DC docs, and the concrete HTML markup shape it will assert is unspecified. This is a new surface on the already-used DC vendor (endpoint granularity): the plan itself notes 'No renderedFields/expand= assertion exists in the harness today', the DC transport has no rendered-fields read method, and no `expand=` usage exists anywhere under tests/external/live_jira_dc. The plan names the render intent (`*foo*`->bold, `h1.`->heading, `{code}`->macro) but not the concrete tags/wrappers DC emits (e.g. bold as `<b>` vs `<strong>`, the heading tag/attributes, the code-macro `<div class="code panel">`/`<pre>` wrapping), so AC1's 'bold/heading/code-macro' assertion could hardcode a shape DC does not produce.
findings.location: Approach (1st bullet, `?expand=renderedFields` HTML assertions) and Acceptance Criteria line 1
scenarios: DC returns renderedFields.description with `<strong>`/`<h1 ...>`/`<div class="code panel ...">` while the test asserts `<b>`/`<h1>`/`<pre>` — the new fidelity check fails in CI for a markup-shape reason, not a bridge defect
DC 8.17.1's `expand=renderedFields` omits or nulls renderedFields for the description field under the PAT/permission context used, and the assertion cannot read the HTML at all
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach/Testing, record the observed DC-8.17.1 renderedFields HTML for each markup (bold, heading, code) from a one-off `dc_request('/rest/api/2/issue/{key}?expand=renderedFields')` probe, and assert on substrings robust to attribute noise (e.g. assert a bold/strong element and the code-macro container class are present) rather than exact tag equality; if the probe cannot be run pre-commit, gate AC1 behind a spike that captures those shapes first.

findings.finding: The live-conflict scenario ('a Jira-side edit between passes keeps rebar's body local-wins AND raises outbound-field-conflict') under-specifies the precondition the cited 3388 policy actually requires: the outbound-field-conflict alert fires only on a BOTH-SIDES divergence (local!=baseline AND remote!=baseline). A bare Jira-side edit with local unchanged is suppressed by the directionality guard and mirrored inbound (Jira-wins) with NO conflict alert.
findings.location: Approach (3rd bullet: 'performs a Jira-side edit'); Testing ('Live conflict'); Acceptance Criteria (2nd checkbox)
findings.suggested_fix: Change the scenario to: (1) converge the body so a baseline is recorded; (2) make a rebar-side local edit to the description AND a Jira-side edit to the same field before the next pass; (3) assert the next pass emits rebar's body (local-wins) and records the deduped outbound-field-conflict:<key>:description alert. This mirrors 3388's test_concurrent_conflict_alerts precondition (local!=baseline AND remote!=baseline).
